newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran hits mock enemy to end largest Gulf wargames.
newsitem.headline: Iran hits mock enemy to end largest Gulf wargames.

text.p: Iranian Revolutionary Guards troops and navy vessels fired live ammunition on Friday to drive a mock enemy from two islands, in the final phase of Iran's largest Gulf wargames, state-run Tehran radio said.
It said 45,000 troops, backed by artillery fire and navy rocket-launchers, defeated "enemy" forces on Qeshm and Hengam islands at the mouth of the Gulf -- conduit for half of the world's oil exports.
The amphibious wargames, codenamed "Tariq ol-Qods" (Road to Jerusalem), ended after successful operations which covered a 400 square-km (150 sq-mile) area, it said.
Planned since last year, the three-day manoeuvres involved 200,000 guards and Basij militia volunteers in operations to test their ability to counter simultaneous threats in Iran's west and south.
They covered 2,000 km (1,200 miles) across four provinces stretching from the mouth of the Gulf to the border with Iraq, Iran's enemy in an eight-year war which ended in 1988.
Tehran has been training the guards, set up after the 1979 Islamic revolution, to become a rapid deployment force.

A U.S. Navy official in the Gulf said earlier the navy was watching the exercises closely, dismissing a Tehran report that U.S. warships had left areas near Iranian waters since the start of the wargames.

Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who is also armed forces commander-in-chief, urged the troops on Thursday to take part in the mock battles as if it they were real, "even though...the probability that events such as these wargames would actually occur is very low".

Khamenei on Tuesday urged Iranians to be vigilant but added that no world power would dare attack Iran. The remarks were an apparent reference to reports the United States might strike if a link was established between Tehran and a bombing last June that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia. Iran denies involvement.
The U.S. navy keeps about 20 warships in the Gulf to enforce sanctions on Iraq and protect Gulf Arab oil states.

Tehran radio said people chanting "Death to America" held a rally on Friday in the central town of Tabas to mark the failure 17 years ago of a U.S. mission to free 52 Americans held hostage by Islamic militants at the U.S. embassy in Tehran.
The operation was aborted on April 25, 1980 after a helicopter collided with a transport aircraft, killing eight U.S. servicemen, during a sandstorm in a desert area outside Tabas.
